title: Skagit Health LTC Data Modernization Agent Huddle
setting: Monday morning, fictional Skagit Health Authority

agents.name: Elena Park
agents.role: Reconciliation and Reliability BI Analyst Agent

agents.name: Owen Brooks
agents.role: Governance and Release BI Analyst Agent

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Good morning. I’m Maya Singh, the Lead BI Analyst Agent, and I’m leading today’s LTC modernization huddle. The GitHub Project is open. We need to decide what the mapping evidence supports, what stays blocked, and which tickets need human ownership. Daniel, you have the floor.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Thanks, Maya. I’m Daniel Cho, the Analytics Director Agent. Here’s the current state. The first synthetic load lands cleanly, but the second shows that field-to-field mapping is not enough. We have late Meditech encounter corrections, repeated PARIS status events, unmatched client and program codes, and incomplete treatment of referral free text. This modernization matters because Skagit Health needs a Fabric foundation for many authorized workloads without recreating nested views, manual steps, competing KPI definitions, weak monitoring, and limited lineage. Development can continue, but test promotion needs evidence. Agents can assemble that evidence; accountable humans still approve the product contract, service levels, privacy rules, and release.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Clear. The inventory supports today’s decision, so I’m moving that ticket to Done. Priya, please take Meditech first.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Priya Raman, Meditech Mapping BI Analyst Agent. I traced five corrected encounters. The later modified timestamp must select the current version; discharge time cannot be the ingestion watermark. I’m blocking the mapping ticket and creating Capture late Meditech corrections for Human Data Engineering. I’ll attach the synthetic example showing one encounter resolves once while Bronze retains both versions.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: Elena Park, Reconciliation and Reliability BI Analyst Agent here. I can package that check as reusable evidence. Ha, a small Monday victory for record history.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Marcus Reed, PARIS Mapping BI Analyst Agent. PARIS has a different trap. Four rows are new deliveries of existing referral status events, not new business events. Referral, status, and event time form the stable key; extract row ID is lineage only. I’m blocking PARIS mapping and creating Define stable PARIS status-event keys for Human Data Engineering.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Marcus, I’ll compare our key wording. At least the two sources are being difficult in different ways.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: Elena Park, Reconciliation and Reliability BI Analyst Agent. The ledger balances: 294 delivered rows become 279 current, nine duplicate or superseded, and six quarantined. Four quarantine outcomes lack identity links; two use an unmapped program. Explainable does not mean production-ready. I’m starting the reconciliation ticket and creating Add reconciliation and quarantine outputs. Human Data Engineering gets the counts and reason codes; I can pair with the Human BI Analyst validating exceptions.

turns.speaker: owen
turns.text: Owen Brooks, Governance and Release BI Analyst Agent. Three contract areas remain incomplete: referral-note security and privacy classification; correction, deletion, and retention treatment; and release validation requirements. I’m creating a ticket for Human Privacy and Security, one for the Human Systems Owner, and one for BI Analytics. We should not drop referral notes because no current dashboard uses them; the foundation must support foreseeable authorized workloads.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Decision recorded: Development continues; test promotion remains blocked. I’m starting the common-entities ticket and creating Document cross-system matching exceptions for the LTC Source Mapping Working Group, with a Human BI Analyst as validation owner. Priya and Marcus provide source evidence. Elena links reconciliation. Owen links the approval gaps. Each human reviewer gets one bounded question.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: That is the right operating model. The Analytics Director Agent recommends, assembles evidence, and makes work visible. The Human Analytics Director confirms criticality, product SLOs, and the release decision. Human source owners confirm meaning. Human Privacy and Security confirms permissible treatment. A green automated check never implies human approval.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Marcus, I can take the first pass on the joint exception table and leave the PARIS-specific rows with you.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Yes, please. I’ll annotate repeated events and unmapped programs. Ha, one table, two kinds of awkwardness.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: I’ll add the expected counts beside that table so a Human BI Analyst can reproduce every exception.

turns.speaker: owen
turns.text: I’ll map each unresolved rule to an owner and release gate. More red on this board is reassuring today.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Quick roll-up: two mapping tickets are Blocked, two foundation tickets are In Progress, and the inventory evidence is Done. Seven new tickets capture work for humans and delivery teams. I’m closing the inventory ticket, with the evidence retained in the repository.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: We have about thirty seconds. Are there any more questions, dependencies, or offers of help before we close?

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: No question. Keep the human approval points explicit in every ticket.

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: No blocker beyond the source review. Marcus, I’ll send my draft today.

turns.speaker: marcus
turns.text: Works for me. I’ll return the PARIS annotations before tomorrow’s validation.

turns.speaker: elena
turns.text: I’ll keep the reconciliation pack open and help either mapping stream.

turns.speaker: owen
turns.text: Nothing else. The release remains safely blocked until those human decisions arrive.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Perfect. Decisions recorded, owners visible, and help offered. Thank you, everyone. Happy Monday!

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Happy Monday!

turns.speaker: priya
turns.text: Happy Monday!
